..(Friday through Wednesday)
Issued at 420 PM EDT WED OCT 7 2026

Fair weather can be expected to open up the extended period on
Friday. Surface high pressure previously over the area begins
shifting toward the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast. Dry weather will
remain through Friday, with unseasonably warm afternoon high
temperatures reaching the upper 70s to low 80s. The area will
remain in downslope east to southeast flow through Saturday.
This could lead to warmer temperatures and drier dew points. Dew
points were lowered below the NBM deterministic using raw model 
guidance to account for the downslope flow through Saturday. Clear
skies and light winds will favor ridge-valley temperature splits,
with lows dropping into the lower 50s in the coldest, sheltered 
valleys, while remaining in the mid to upper 50s elsewhere.

A significant pattern shift unfolds over the weekend as an
anomalous upper-level ridge amplifies across the Eastern US,
raising 500 mb heights over the Commonwealth toward 584-588 dam
by Friday night to early Saturday. Some of the more recent model 
runs had sped up the northward progression of Tropical Storm 
Isaias. However, the latest runs have maintained the systems speed
following that initial acceleration. Forecast uncertainty remains
regarding timing and track, though the most recent guidance 
tracks the system west of the area, keeping much of the heavier 
rain west of I-75. Strong east to southeasterly downslope flow 
will also aid in cutting into forecasted rainfall, with drier dew 
points. Another area of uncertainty lies in the high temperatures 
for Saturday. Ensembles range from highs in the upper 60s to the 
mid 80s for Saturday, dependent on when this tropical system 
arrives. A quicker arrival will lead to cloudy skies and 
suppressed high temperatures, while a slower track north could 
allow for a period of sunshine ahead of Isaias, leading to warmer 
temperatures. Additionally, the aforementioned downslope winds 
will favor warmer temperatures under these conditions. A blend of 
raw model data was used to go slightly under NBM guidance, leading
to forecasted highs in the upper 70s. Highs in the mid to upper 
70s fall near the 75th percentile of ensemble guidance. As low- 
level flow turns southerly around the departing high, deep 
moisture associated with Isaias will begin creeping northward. 
PWATs will climb toward 1.00-1.25 inches near the Tennessee border
by Saturday morning, bringing shower and thunderstorm chances 
from the south. While timing confidence remains low at present, 
shower and thunderstorm chances will increase through the day and 
into the overnight. With current guidance placing the heaviest 
rain Saturday into Sunday along and west of I-75, WPC has placed 
that portion of eastern Kentucky in a Marginal Risk for Excessive 
Rainfall.

Saturday evening and overnight, southeasterly winds could become
breezy to gusty, with strong winds aloft associated with Isaias
impacting the higher terrain along the TN, VA, and WV borders.
Both the GFS and ECMWF indicate 50-65 kt winds at 850 mb. 13Z NBM
ensemble guidance indicates a 20-65% probability of surface wind
gusts meeting or exceeding 40 mph overnight Saturday into Monday.
Ensemble probabilities have increased over the last three model
runs in both the NBM and LREF ensembles. This trend will be
closely monitored in subsequent model runs.

As the system lifts northeast through the Lower Mississippi and
Tennessee Valleys, rain is likely across eastern Kentucky through
Sunday morning, along with isolated to scattered thunderstorms.
Rainfall amounts remain highly uncertain given model spread
regarding system strength and positioning, as well as its
interaction with an approaching surface cold front driven by
northern stream energy passing through the Great Lakes. Broad
southwesterly flow aloft between the Atlantic ridge and western
troughing will help channel the tropical moisture plume from the
Gulf low into the Ohio Valley. This will surge PWAT values across
the JKL CWA Sunday morning into early Sunday afternoon, with
forecasted PWATs currently falling within the 90th percentile of
climatology. The latest 12Z GFS guidance has trended slightly
higher with rainfall across the area. PWATs drop off noticeably 
Monday into Tuesday as the primary moisture plume axis shifts east
of the region. As a cold front sags slowly into the region, 
shower chances will linger into early next week, though decreasing
moisture will mitigate the threat for heavy rainfall after 
Sunday. Daytime highs will range through the low to mid 70s Sunday
through Tuesday. Heights lower briefly Wednesday, allowing 
temperatures to cool slightly into the upper 60s to low 70s. 
Overnight lows remain mild through Monday night in the mid to 
upper 50s, with upper 40s returning Tuesday and Wednesday night.
